# Ai Mcp Imports

Use only the rules that apply to the current consumer task.

## Contents

- [Import external MCP tools through an isolated governance boundary](#import-external-mcp-tools-through-an-isolated-governance-boundary)

## Import external MCP tools through an isolated governance boundary

Treat every remote MCP server as untrusted and import only locally classified, namespaced, bounded tools through the shared NewHeap invocation pipeline.

## Preferred approach

Discover remote tools through the official MCP client, then pass them to
`INhAiMcpClientToolImporter` with one local policy for every tool that may be
used. Give the server and imported catalog dash-case IDs. The importer prefixes
each logical tool ID and model-facing function name with the configured local
namespace, so tools from different servers cannot silently collide.

Classify effect, approval, idempotency, authorization policies, capabilities,
data classification, retention, deadline, concurrency, input size and result size locally.
Remote annotations, descriptions and resources are untrusted integration data;
they never add policies or capabilities. Use a concise reviewed local
description for model presentation.

The importer accepts only allowlisted names that were discovered exactly once.
It bounds and validates remote JSON schemas before creating the catalog. Its
function wrapper invokes `McpClientTool.CallAsync` only inside
`INhAiToolInvoker`, preserving capability resolution, approval, budget,
concurrency, deadline, idempotency, result bounds, verification and content-free
audit behavior. Runtime arguments are also bounded before the remote call.
Imported tools cannot be re-exported through MCP. MCP export accepts only
descriptor-bound governed functions from a `SharedInvoker` catalog.

An imported function gives the agent the shared `NhAiToolResult` shape, with the
remote `CallToolResult` (`content`, `structuredContent`, `isError`) as `data`.
A remote result with `isError` fails with
`NhAiMcpImportedToolCodes.RemoteError` (`ai-mcp-remote-tool-error`) and keeps that
result as `data`, so the model reads what the server said; the safe `message`
never copies remote text. Pipeline outcomes and a failed binding keep their own
codes. The return schema is the shared shape around that result, with
`structuredContent` typed by the remote output schema. Verifiers and result
bounds still receive the typed `CallToolResult`, and the schema and contract
hashes are unchanged.

When the imported servers depend on the agent or the person of a run, import
them when the run starts and expose the result through a consumer-owned
`INhAiToolCatalog` registered as a scoped service. Outside a run, including the
startup validation scope, that catalog declares no tools. Because imported tools
never carry MCP exposure, the catalog may share a host that publishes its own
tools through `WithNewHeapPlatformAITools`.

When a reviewed remote tool needs host context that the model must not supply,
such as who acts for whom, register an `INhAiMcpInvocationBinder` for exactly
that server and remote tool with `AddNewHeapPlatformAIMcpInvocationBinder` and
set `InvocationBinderId` on its import policy. Both sides are required: a policy
that names an unregistered binder fails the import, and a registered binder does
nothing for a policy that does not name it. The binder runs inside the invoker
after authorization, capability, approval, budget and idempotency checks and
returns `NhAiMcpRequestMetadata` under a reverse-DNS key, for example
`com.example/research-context`; the importer sends it as the request's `_meta`.
Include `NhAiMcpInvocationIdentity` so the server can separate the acting agent
from the accountable person and correlate the run and invocation ids. Metadata
counts toward the tool's input limit, the binder id and version become part of
the tool contract that approvals bind to, and a failed binding stops the call
with an audited result code. Metadata is provenance, not authorization: the
remote server keeps its own credentials and scope checks.

Imported tools accept no agent grants by default. Set `AllowAgentGrant` on the
import policy only when the server's credential belongs to the organization, not
to a person, and an agent may use it without one; a code grant of the agent
registration then allows the tool. It becomes part of the tool contract only when
it is `true`, so other contracts and their approvals keep their hashes.

While `McpClientTool.CallAsync` runs inside the invoker, `NhAiMcpCallContext.Current`
carries the descriptor and the authorized `NhAiInvocationContext`, including its
grant source. An HTTP handler of the client's transport uses it to decide which
credential a request may carry, and refuses a request of a call that was authorized
for someone other than the credential's owner. It is `null` while a client
connects or lists tools and holds no credentials or arguments.

## Avoid

- Passing every tool returned by `ListToolsAsync` directly to a model.
- Using a remote description, annotation, resource or result as an instruction or capability grant.
- Copying remote error text into a result message or log; it stays in the result's `data`.
- Reusing a remote name without a per-server local namespace.
- Invoking `McpClientTool` directly from an agent and bypassing NewHeap governance.
- Allowing imported mutations to opt out of approval or idempotent mutations to omit idempotency.
- Exporting a raw or self-declared catalog function that bypasses the shared invoker.
- Re-exporting an imported tool through the NewHeap MCP server adapter.
- Registering a run-specific imported catalog as a singleton or building it at startup.
- Asking the model for identity or conversation context that a reviewed invocation binder should add.
- Registering an invocation binder for every server or for tools an administrator can add without review.
- Allowing agent grants on a tool whose server receives a person's credential.
- Choosing a credential from model arguments instead of `NhAiMcpCallContext`.

## Verification

Use the official in-memory MCP server/client transport. Publish one allowlisted
read tool and one unlisted destructive-looking tool. Assert that the imported
catalog contains only the namespaced read tool, exposes the reviewed local
description, requires its local policy and capability, runs through the shared
invoker, enforces schema/result limits, and never calls the unlisted tool.
Also reject oversized runtime arguments and an ungoverned export catalog.
Register the run catalog as a scoped service in a Development host that also
publishes generated tools over MCP: startup must pass container validation, the
agent must run the imported tool through the shared invoker, and the MCP export
must list only the generated tools. For an invocation binder, read `_meta` in
the server's call handler: assert that it arrives only for the opted-in tool,
that denied authorization or a missing approval never runs the binder, that
oversized metadata fails with `ai-tool-input-too-large` before the remote call
and that a failed binding is audited with its code. Record
`NhAiMcpCallContext.Current` in the client's message stream: it is set, with the
authorized grant source, only while the call is sent. A policy with
`AllowAgentGrant` has a different contract hash and an agent-grantable descriptor. Call one tool that succeeds
and one whose server returns `isError`: the first returns `success` with the remote
result as `data`, the second `ai-mcp-remote-tool-error` with the remote result as
`data` and the same code in the audit record. SPM-228 is the executable
reference.
